chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:
I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) about this Verse: 'Nor is there blame on you that you eat from your houses, or your fathers' houses or your mothers' houses' – the Verse.
He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no blame on you regarding what you eat and consume from what you possess its keys, as long as you do not spoil it.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ: No blame or sin is upon you

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic verse 'Nor is there blame on you that you eat from your houses' mean according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (or al-Baqir) interprets Quran 24:61 by linking the permissibility of eating in others' houses to the concept of possessing the keys (mala' al-mafatih), thereby extending the scope beyond just one's own home to any residence under one's control. This exegetical nuance highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical ownership and consent as conditions for lawful consumption, reinforcing the principle that permission is implied through access and lack of spoilage. It serves as a foundational text for understanding domestic rights and hospitality in Islamic jurisprudence.
